terms.gloss: a vehicle, a carriage, a cart
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 3.5.28: mihi aequum est darī vehicula, quī vehar (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Any means of carrying, from vehō: a wagon or cart, a carriage, once even a ship (Cic. Verr. 2.5.59, Lewis & Short). Traupman keeps it for road vehicles in general: commeātus vehiculōrum, traffic (174, 397), cavē statuās vehiculum!, no parking (217).

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. vectūra: a conveying, carrying

phrases.latin: comes fācundus in viā prō vehiculō est
phrases.english: a good talker on the road is as good as a carriage

phrases.latin: mihi aequum est darī vehicula, quī vehar
phrases.english: it’s only fair I should be given a carriage to ride in

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 174, 217, 397, checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.
